# The least CS congruence is generated by comparable idempotents

**Status: NEW AUTHOR WRITTEN GENERAL PROOF plus exact finite control; UNREVIEWED / UNADOPTED.** Likely classical: no novelty is asserted. This gives explicit generators and a direct proof for the least CS quotient, without using the universal group presentation or an intersection of all quotient maps. It does not prove physical-band SEP/R/L.

## 1. Exact theorem

For any nonempty regular semigroup S, let θ be the congruence generated by all pairs `(e,f)` of idempotents satisfying `ef=fe=e`. Then `S/θ` is completely simple and θ is the least CS congruence ν.

Every homomorphism to a CS semigroup identifies comparable idempotents because the natural order on its idempotents is equality. Thus `θ⊆ν`. To prove equality it suffices to show S/θ is CS; the proof below works for finite or infinite S.

## 2. Quotient idempotents have equality natural order

Write U=S/θ and π:S→U. U is regular. If `ε≤φ` are idempotents of U, lift φ to an idempotent f∈S. This standard regular-source lift is explicit: choose x with π(x)=φ and an inverse z of x²; then xzx is idempotent and maps to φ.

Since `ε=φ ε φ`, choose y∈S with π(y)=ε and put x=fyf∈fSf, so π(x)=ε. The local monoid fSf is regular: if x∈fSf has an inner inverse v in S, then fvf is an inner inverse inside fSf, and its standard reflexive adjustment gives a mutual inverse there. Choose an inverse z of x² inside fSf. Then `k=xzx` is an idempotent of fSf with π(k)=ε. As k,f are idempotents and k∈fSf, `kf=fk=k`. Thus k θ f is one of the generating comparable pairs, yielding ε=φ. Therefore U has equality as its natural order on idempotents.

No assumption that π is pure or idempotent-separating was used in this lifting argument.

## 3. A regular semigroup with no comparable distinct idempotents is CS

Take any idempotents ε,φ∈U. Put p=εφ and take a mutual inverse v of p. The elements

`a=pvε`, `b=φvp`

are idempotent and satisfy a≤ε, b≤φ. For example `a²=pv ε p v ε=pv p v ε=pvε=a`, and both aε=a and εa=a; the dual calculation gives b. Equality natural order forces `pvε=ε`, `φvp=φ`. The first equality and p=εφ show `p R ε`; the second shows `p L φ`. Thus all idempotents of U lie in one D-class. Every regular element is R-related to one idempotent and L-related to another, so U has one D-class and hence is simple. Its idempotents are primitive (there are none strictly below them); by Rees–Suschkewitsch, U is completely simple.

Consequently θ itself is a CS congruence and ν⊆θ. Combined with §1, θ=ν. □

## 4. Finite computation and a nonorthodox exact control

For finite S of size n, list its idempotents and every strict comparable pair. Generate a congruence by a union-find worklist: whenever x,y merge, also merge `sx,sy` and `xs,ys` for every source s, until no new merge occurs. At most n−1 nontrivial merges occur; each emits at most2n translation-pairs, in addition to at most n² seeds. Thus, with path-compressed union-find and dense source table lookup, this computes ν in O(n²·α(n)) union/find work after the pair list (up to fixed bookkeeping), without enumerating Bell(n) partitions or group words. This complexity is for the least-CS congruence only, not the canonical band or the all-host decision.
